facts.claim: 1676 콘웰 석회암 채석장 — 메갈로사우루스 넓적다리뼈 일부
facts.note: Part of a bone, now known to have been the femur of a Megalosaurus, was recovered from a limestone quarry at Cornwell near Chipping Norton, Oxfordshire, in 1676.

facts.claim: 1841 강연에선 말하지 않고 1842년 4월 원고에서 Dinosauria 도입
facts.note: Owen had given a presentation about fossil reptiles to the British Association for the Advancement of Science in 1841, but reports of the time show that Owen did not mention the word "dinosaur" ... He introduced the Dinosauria only in the revised text version of his talk published in April 1842.
The fragment was sent to Robert Plot ... He therefore concluded it to be the femur of a huge human, perhaps a Titan or another type of giant featured in legends.

Plot's engraving of the Cornwell bone was again used in a book by Richard Brookes in 1763. Brookes, in a caption, called it "Scrotum humanum", apparently comparing its appearance to a pair of "human testicles".

question.hintNote: Megalosaurus was named in 1824 by William Buckland, becoming the first genus of dinosaur to be validly named (other than birds, not then recognized as dinosaurs).

facts.note: French palaeontologist Marcellin Boule, who authored several publications starting in 1908 describing the French Neanderthal specimen La Chapelle-aux-Saints 1 ("The Old Man") as a slouching, ape-like creature distantly related to modern man.
